battle.name: 黃巢之亂
battle.theater: 河南陝西（潼關至長安一線）
battle.brief: 乾符二年（875年）浙西睦州起事，王仙芝、黃巢以鹽幫為骨幹，轉戰江南嶺南。廣明元年冬義軍連破洛陽、潼關，十二月入長安建大齊。883年沙陀李克用率騎兵入關，義軍西走，884年黃巢死於泰山狼虎谷，大齊覆亡。卡面埃及長矛並非戰中裝備，義軍步卒的長矛與短刀才是亂軍最普遍的近戰兵器。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 唐末這場動亂的交戰方是兩層結構：義軍一方與唐廷一方，而唐廷一方本身又分成中央直屬與割據節度使兩層。義軍一方最初沒有國號，也沒有固定編制，骨幹是浙西睦州、婺州一帶的私鹽幫眾與流民。乾符二年（875年）睦州人陳反、趙辯、鄭端等聚眾起事，推河南販私鹽出身的王仙芝為首；王仙芝陣亡後由曹州冤句人黃巢收拾餘眾，旗號仍帶「天兵」意味，直到廣明元年（880年）十二月進軍長安才建立大齊，改元金統，黃巢自稱皇帝，並分封尚讓、林言、張林等為各處節度使，實際上是一個以主帥為唯一中心的軍事集團，而非常規的王朝編制。義軍的作戰單位是「隊」，隊下設「夥」，再下為「卒」；兵源除鹽幫與饑民外，還有被裹挾的役夫、逃戶與散兵，紀律鬆散而人數眾多，這一點在作戰方式上留下明顯烙印。唐廷一方以皇帝為最高統帥，實權卻分散在宦官的監軍與各道節度使手中。黃巢出河南時，朝廷能直接指揮的只有神策軍等少數禁軍與若干藩鎮援軍，兵將互不相屬，糧餉各出自本鎮，這是初期屢敗之因。廣明元年僖宗出幸成都，藩鎮觀望，朝廷幾乎喪失全部作戰能力。中和二年（882年）起，河中節度使王重榮與諸道聯兵進逼，僖宗被迫下詔，許節度使自署招討使、兼御史中丞以統兵討巢，換取出兵；中和三年（883年）末各道兵馬名義上歸節度使節制，實際上互相觀望，聯軍逼近長安時仍有各懷異心者。中間地帶是地方團練與土豪武裝，兩面應付，往往先與義軍往來再倒向官軍，這是叛軍能長期周旋的原因之一。
countriesEn: The two sides in this upheaval at the end of the Tang were arranged in two layers: the insurgents on one hand, and the Tang court on the other, and the court itself was itself split between the central armies directly under the throne and the regional military governors. The insurgent side had at first no state name and no fixed organisation; its backbone was the private-salt smugglers' bands and the displaced people of the Mouchang and Wuzhou area in western Zhejiang. In the second year of Qianfeng, 875, men from Mouchang named Chen Fan, Zhao Bian and Zheng Duan gathered a crowd and rose, and pushed forward Wang Xianzhi, who sold salt illicitly in Henan, as their leader. After Wang Xianzhi fell in battle, Huang Chao, a native of Yuanjue in Caozhou, gathered up the survivors; their banner still carried the character of a rising against the throne under the sign of heavenly soldiers, and it was not until they entered Chang'an in the twelfth month of Guangming, 880, that they proclaimed the Great Qi, changed the era to Jintong, and set Huang Chao up as emperor, with Shang Rang, Lin Yan and Zhang Lin appointed to seats of military authority in various regions. In practice this was a military group with a single commander at its centre rather than a regular dynastic organisation. The tactical unit of the insurgents was the dui, below it the huo, and below that the zu. Their manpower came not only from the salt bands and the hungry, but also from press-ganged corvée labourers, tax fugitives and loose soldiers; discipline was loose and numbers were large, and this left a clear mark on the way they fought. On the court side the emperor was the supreme commander in form, but real power lay with eunuch supervisors and with the military governors of the circuits. When Huang Chao came out of Henan, the only troops the court could directly command were a handful of imperial guards such as the Shence Army together with contingents from a few governors; the troops and commanders did not belong to one another and each drew its pay and grain from its own circuit, and this was why the early campaigns failed. When the emperor fled to Chengdu in the first year of Guangming, the governors looked on and the court very nearly lost all capacity to fight. From 882 the circuit governor of Hezhong, Wang Chongrong, and the armies of several circuits pressed on the court, and the emperor was forced to issue an edict allowing the governors to style themselves as commissioners for suppression and to hold the additional office of censor-in-chief, in exchange for putting troops in the field. By the end of 883 the troops of the circuits nominally came under the governors, but in practice each watched the others, and even as the coalition closed on Chang'an there were still commanders nursing their own designs. Between the two sides lay the local militia and the armed households of the strong local families, who served whichever side they could and often dealt with the insurgents before turning to the court; this was one reason the rebellion could keep moving for so long.
people: 留下姓名的，多數在唐廷一方，義軍一方留下姓名的並不多。黃巢（約835至884年），曹州冤句人，鹽幫首領，售私鹽為業，傳說他曾應進士科不第，落第之後寫下〈不第後賦〉。乾符二年起事時，他只是王仙芝麾下一支力量的帶頭人；王仙芝乾符四年（877年）在河南渦口一帶戰死，餘眾推黃巢為首，此後數年間他由一支流寇的首領變成自建政權的皇帝，廣明元年進長安，號大齊，年號金統，尊號承天應運啟聖睿文宣武皇帝。中和三年（883年）關中決戰失利，他焚長安宮室西走，次年光啟元年（884年）六月兵敗於泰山狼虎谷，與殘部數百人一同覆滅，與其子黃邈走散。王仙芝（？至877年），河南人，私鹽販子出身，起義之初所聚不過千人，其後眾至數萬，是唐廷眼中最難對付的首領；他死後部眾分散，才有了黃巢獨力支撐的局面。尚讓是義軍最核心的將領，正是他在長安力勸黃巢稱帝；建國之後又統軍出關與官軍對峙，中和三年他率大軍拒李克用於關中，兵敗之後收拾散卒繼續抵抗，直至光啟年間為官軍所擒殺。黃巢的外甥林言與尚讓同為大將，廣明元年十二月奇襲潼關側翼的禁阬，造成官軍崩潰，直接打開入關之路。唐廷方面，河東節度使李克用是最關鍵的人物：沙陀人，父卓落死於軍中，他以善使鐵槊、驍騎剽悍著稱，中和三年率沙陀騎兵與河東兵入關，擊潰尚讓大軍於關中，追黃巢至泰山，此後受封晉王，成為唐末最具實力的藩鎮之一。朱溫原為義軍將領，後歸唐，被授以宣武軍的地盤，成為後來取代唐朝的關鍵人物。河中節度使王重榮在882至883年間聯絡諸道逼宮，使朝廷不得不下詔諸道討巢，功在引來官軍，也在藩鎮坐大中扮演了極重要的角色。宦官田令孜掌神策軍，護駕出奔，在潼關之敗中與守將張承範互相掣肘，其後又倚仗李克用平亂，權力更盛。陳反、趙辯、鄭端是875年睦州起義的首倡者；秦宗權原為蔡州奉國軍節度使，先降義軍而後再度反叛，是黃巢死後最難平息的餘波。
peopleEn: Most of the names that survive belong to the court side; the insurgents left behind far fewer. Huang Chao, who lived from about 835 to 884, was a native of Yuanjue in Caozhou and the chief of a salt band, earning his living selling salt outside the monopoly; according to tradition he sat the metropolitan examination and failed, and wrote his poem On Failing the Examination afterward. When the rising began in 875 he led only one contingent under Wang Xianzhi; when Wang fell at Wokou in Henan in 877, the survivors made Huang their leader, and within a few years he turned from the head of a roving band into the ruler of a state of his own, entering Chang'an in 880 under the name of the Great Qi, with the era Jintong and the title Emperor Chengtian Yingyun Qisheng Ruiwen Xuanwu. When he lost the decisive engagement in Guanzhong in 883 he fired the palaces of Chang'an and withdrew west, and in the sixth month of 884 he was destroyed at Langhu Valley below Mount Tai with some several hundred of his remaining men, scattering from his son Huang Miao. Wang Xianzhi, who died in 877, was a native of Henan who had sold salt outside the monopoly; his following was no more than a thousand men when he rose and grew to tens of thousands, and he was the single hardest opponent the court had to deal with; once he was dead his bands scattered, and only then did Huang Chao carry the movement alone. Shang Rang was the most central of the insurgent commanders, and it was he who pressed Huang Chao to take the throne at Chang'an; after the state was proclaimed he led the army out of the passes to face the court, and in 883 he brought the main body to oppose Li Keyong in Guanzhong, gathering up the stragglers and continuing to resist after his defeat until he was taken and killed by the court's troops in the Guangming years. Lin Yan, Huang Chao's nephew, was a general alongside Shang Rang, and in the twelfth month of 880 he seized the fortified post on the flank of the Tong Pass by surprise, causing the government army to collapse and opening the road into the passes. On the court side the decisive figure was the governor of Hedong, Li Keyong. A Shatuo man whose father Zhuoluo had died in service, he was famed for his skill with the iron spear and for the hard riding of his troops; in 883 he entered the passes with Shatuo cavalry and the armies of Hedong, shattered Shang Rang's army in Guanzhong and pursued Huang Chao as far as Mount Tai, and was later enfeoffed as Prince of Jin, becoming one of the most powerful governors of the late Tang. Zhu Wen had been a general of the insurgents before he came over to the court, and was granted the territory of Xuanwu, which made him the key figure in the dynasty's eventual replacement. Wang Chongrong, governor of Hezhong, coordinated the various circuits in 882 and 883 and pressed the court until it issued the edict calling on the circuits to suppress the rebels; his part in drawing the government army into the war was important, and so was his part in the swelling of the governors' power. The eunuch Tian Lingzi commanded the Shence Army and escorted the emperor in his flight; at the loss of Tong Pass he quarrelled and obstructed the defending commander Zhang Chengfan, and afterwards, resting on Li Keyong to put the rebellion down, his authority grew still further. Chen Fan, Zhao Bian and Zheng Duan were the first movers of the rising at Mouchang in 875. Qin Zongquan, governor of the Fengguo Army at Caizhou, first surrendered to the insurgents and then rebelled again, and he was the most persistent of the aftermaths left by Huang Chao's death.
kits: 先要說清楚一件容易誤讀的事：卡面上的這把埃及長矛，並沒有隨義軍出現在中國。它是埃及早王朝時期就有的近身兵器，銅或青銅矛頭安在木杆上，早期用來守城垣，後來也用於收復失地。把它放進黃巢之亂的裝備表，是因為它屬於「長柄穿刺」這一條最古老技術路線的祖型，而義軍步卒手中的長矛，正是同一條路線在唐末的另一個分支。唐末兵器的骨幹是長柄器與刀：步卒最普遍的是矛與槊，矛為直刃，槊為兩側有刃的長柄兵器，都以刺擊為主；軍中同時有陌刀與環首直刃刀，前者用於劈砍，後者拔出省力。遠射以弓為主，用鐵箭鏃，弩則有臂弩與拉力更大者，配箭袋與機括，是攻城與守城時的常備。甲胄方面，官軍以皮甲與札甲為主，重要將領才有金屬鎧甲，義軍多無甲或只有粗布纏身，臨陣以盾與拒馬木為倚仗。攻城與守城的器材包括雲梯、撞車、投石用的砲、穴地用的木版與鍬、火箭與火油，用來燒灼城門與城上的遮蔽物，另有木製的攻城塔。運輸靠馬、驢、牛，車多為牛車，軍中大量使用從州縣繳獲的車馬，渡水則依賴舟船與臨時編成的渡河隊。兩件與卡面兵器直接相關的細節值得記下：李克用所部沙陀騎兵最重裝備是長柄鐵槊，騎在馬上以槊刺穿，這是唐末最有效的騎兵近戰兵器；義軍步卒的長矛則多為竹木杆加裝鐵刃，甚至有用農具改製者，因亂軍缺乏統一製式，裝備雜亂難辨。較之卡面的埃及銅矛，唐末的矛已完全是鐵器時代的產物，但握持方式、刺擊邏輯與列陣位置，幾千年來幾無二致。
kitsEn: One thing has to be said first, because it is easy to misread: the Egyptian spear on the card did not march with the insurgents into China. It was a close-combat weapon the Egyptians had used since the Old Kingdom, a copper or bronze head fitted to a wooden shaft, employed at first to hold city walls and later to recover lost ground. It belongs in the equipment table of Huang Chao's rebellion because it is the ancestor type of one very old line of technique, the thrusting pole, and the spears in the hands of the insurgents' foot soldiers are precisely a branch of that same line at the end of the Tang. The backbone of late Tang arms was the pole weapon and the blade. The commonest items in the hands of the foot were the mao and the shuo, the first with a straight point and the second a long shaft with blades on both sides, both used primarily to thrust; the army also carried the modao, the broad sword for chopping, and the ring-pommel straight sword, which could be drawn out of a body without twisting. Missile weapons were chiefly the bow with iron arrowheads, with crossbows of the shoulder type and of greater draw as well, carried with quivers and triggers, standard equipment for both assault and defence of walls. For armour, the government troops relied on leather and on lamellar protection, with metal harness for important commanders only; the insurgents for the most part had none, or only coarse cloth wound round the body, and depended in the line on shields and on wooden abatis. The tools of siege and of defence included scaling ladders, battering rams, stone-throwers, wooden planks and spades for driving tunnels, fire arrows and fire oil for burning gates and the screens above them, and wooden siege towers. Movement depended on horses, mules and oxen, with ox carts for transport; the armies made large use of wagons and beasts taken from the counties they overran, and rivers were crossed by boats and by hastily organised ferry parties. Two details bear directly on the weapon on the card. The heaviest weapon carried by Li Keyong's Shatuo cavalry was the long iron shuo, thrust from horseback, and it was the most effective close-combat arm of late Tang cavalry; the insurgents' foot spears, by contrast, were mostly bamboo or wooden shafts fitted with iron blades, and some were converted farm tools, for the rebel armies had no standard issue and their equipment was confused to the eye. Compared with the Egyptian copper spear on the card, the Tang spear is entirely a product of the iron age; yet the way it is gripped, the logic of the thrust and the place it holds in the order of battle have changed very little in several thousand years.
tactics: 義軍的戰術可以用四個詞概括：流動、避實、破城、就食。流動是根本：義軍從不打算固守一城，攻克之後即棄之，取其糧、其財、其馬匹而退，轉向下一處兵力薄弱或民政空虛的州縣，行軍多取小道，避開官軍主力所在的大道。避實擊虛是其打法的核心，正面對抗節度使的精兵沒有勝算，只有趁各鎮彼此不相援、挑其薄弱處下手，才可能連續攻城。破城之後就地取糧是維持這支數萬人隊伍的唯一辦法，史載義軍所過州縣「倉庫一空」，這既使義軍得以維持，也使沿線地方再無守軍可恃。攻城手段與唐軍並無二致：雲梯、撞木、穴地、堆土為山，以火攻配合，並臨時徵用城內的工匠與攻城器；義軍的優勢在於器具多為臨時製造、講究不多，劣勢則在缺少能固守的防禦器械，一旦攻城不克即退。唐軍方面，節度使各守其地，兵將互不相屬，配合極差，潼關之敗正出於此：守關諸軍分屬不同將領，命令不一，黃巢部將林言、尚讓奇襲側翼的禁阬，官軍腹背受敵，全軍崩潰，僖宗出奔成都以後，關中再無能作戰之師。883年關中再戰，情形完全不同：李克用把沙陀驍騎放在最前，以騎兵衝陣，唐廷集中於華州、渭水一線的各鎮兵為其後援，義軍雖眾而無騎兵，難以承受衝撞，十五萬眾在接戰之後即告瓦解。此役之後，戰局由攻勢轉為追擊，李克用追奔至泰山，黃巢以殘兵拒守狼虎谷而全軍覆沒。這場戰爭的勝負，最後是在騎兵與步兵的對比上定下來的。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the insurgents can be summed up in four words: movement, avoiding the strong, storming the city, and living off the country. Movement was the foundation. The insurgents never intended to hold a city; having taken it they would leave it, taking its grain, its wealth and its horses, and turn towards the next county or prefecture where the garrison was thin or the administration hollow. On the march they used small roads, avoiding the great highways along which the main government forces lay. Avoiding the strong and striking the weak was the core of their method, for they had no prospect against the picked troops of a military governor in open battle; only by taking advantage of the fact that the circuits did not support one another and striking where the defence was thinnest could they take city after city. Living off the country after the city fell was the only way to keep an army of tens of thousands in the field; the record says the granaries of the counties they passed were emptied, which sustained the rebels and at the same time left the districts along the line with no troops left to defend them. Their siege methods were no different from those of the government armies: scaling ladders, battering rams, tunnels, earthen ramps raised against the wall, fire attacks, and the hasty use of the craftsmen and siege gear found inside the city. Their strength lay in gear that was roughly made and hastily put together; their weakness lay in having nothing that could hold a position, so that a failed assault meant an immediate withdrawal. On the government side, each governor sat in his own circuit, troops and commanders belonged to no one but themselves, and cooperation was extremely poor; the loss of Tong Pass was exactly that. The troops defending the pass were under different commanders, orders did not match, Lin Yan and Shang Rang of the rebel army seized the fortified post on the flank by surprise, the government force was taken between two fires and collapsed, and after the emperor fled to Chengdu there was no longer any army in Guanzhong able to fight. The second engagement in Guanzhong in 883 was a different matter altogether. Li Keyong put the Shatuo horse at the head, the cavalry charging the line, with the assembled circuits of the court behind them along the Huan and Wei fronts. The rebels were numerous but had no horse, could not absorb the impact, and their reported one hundred and fifty thousand broke up as soon as contact was made. After that engagement the war changed from offensive to pursuit; Li Keyong pursued them to Mount Tai, and Huang Chao, with the remnants, was cornered at Langhu Valley and destroyed. The outcome of this war was settled, in the end, on the comparison between cavalry and infantry.
data: 可核對的數字分三類，來源可靠程度相差很大。第一類是文獻與史書的記載。年份：起事在乾符二年，即875年；王仙芝死於乾符四年，877年；黃巢建大齊在廣明元年，880年；李克用入關收復長安在中和三年，883年；黃巢死於光啟元年，884年；若計入殘部與秦宗權至889年前後方告平定，整場動亂前後延續十數年。月份：乾符二年七月浙西起事，廣明元年十二月黃巢軍入長安。兵力：史書記黃巢出嶺南時自報「四十萬」，這類亂軍自報的人數通常要打上數折折扣；中和三年黃巢遣尚讓率兵十五萬拒李克用於關中，而李克用入關之兵約五萬，其中沙陀騎兵為骨幹；黃巢敗亡之時所部已不滿千餘。距離：自嶺南廣州到關中長安，直線距離約一千五百餘公里，實際行軍因避開官軍與攻取城池而遠遠更長。第二類是地理與制度上可數的量。黃巢北上的主要節點可以數出來：福州、廣州、洛陽、潼關、長安，其間在江西、浙江、江淮轉戰的州縣不計其數；起義的地理核心則是睦州、婺州一帶的鹽井區。鹽法上的關鍵數字是：唐室在浙西睦州、婺州設有鹽井與鹽監，鹽戶本身服役，鄉戶須繳納代納的鹽利，兩稅法施行之後稅額與鹽利歸併，負擔多落在無鹽之地的小農身上。第三類是推估，必須打折：唐末朝廷常備軍與各鎮兵力的總數，說法從數十萬到上百萬不等，難以核實；所謂「四十萬」「十五萬」多屬統帥誇大之辭，實際作戰兵力在數萬量級。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes of very different reliability. The first class is what the documents and the standard histories record. The years: the rising began in the second year of Qianfeng, 875; Wang Xianzhi died in the fourth year of Qianfeng, 877; Huang Chao founded the Great Qi in the first year of Guangming, 880; Li Keyong entered the passes and retook Chang'an in the third year of Zhonghe, 883; Huang Chao died in the first year of Guangqi, 884; and if the remnants and Qin Zongquan are counted, the disturbance ran on for a dozen years or more before it was finally settled in 889. The months: the rising in western Zhejiang fell in the seventh month of Qianfeng, and Huang Chao's army entered Chang'an in the twelfth month of Guangming. Strength: the histories record that when Huang Chao set out from Lingnan he claimed forty thousand, and such figures, self-reported by a rebel army, normally have to be discounted several times over. In 883 Huang Chao sent Shang Rang with one hundred and fifty thousand to oppose Li Keyong in Guanzhong, while the force with which Li Keyong entered the passes was about fifty thousand, the Shatuo horse being its backbone; by the time Huang Chao was destroyed his command was down to less than a thousand. Distance: from Guangzhou in Lingnan to Chang'an in Guanzhong is roughly fifteen hundred kilometres in a straight line, and the actual march was much longer because it had to avoid the government armies and to take cities on the way. The second class consists of countable quantities of geography and institution. The main waypoints of Huang Chao's march north can be enumerated: Fuzhou, Guangzhou, Luoyang, Tong Pass and Chang'an, not counting the prefectures and counties fought over in Jiangxi, Zhejiang and the Huai-Yangtze region; the geographical core of the rising was the salt-well district around Mouchang and Wuzhou. The decisive figures in the salt system are these: the Tang maintained salt wells and salt offices at Mouchang and Wuzhou in western Zhejiang, the salt households themselves served, the ordinary households paid salt dues in lieu, and after the two-tax system was introduced the tax and the salt profit were merged, so that the burden fell mostly on small farmers in places that had no salt at all. The third class is estimate, and must be discounted: figures for the total size of the Tang's standing forces and of the circuits' armies range from tens of thousands to over a million and cannot be checked; the so-called forty thousand and one hundred and fifty thousand are for the most part the exaggerations of commanders, and the real fighting strength was on the order of tens of thousands.
cause: 打起來的原因可以分成三層。最表層是浙西的饑荒與鹽法。乾符二年江南穀物歉收，饑民大量流入浙東；而唐室在睦州、婺州一帶設有鹽井與鹽監，專賣之利是當時財政的重要支柱，鹽戶服役、鄉戶分擔，兩稅法推行後鹽利與稅額合併加重，負擔落到無鹽之地的小農身上。民間販私鹽本是這個體系的縫隙，朝廷查禁越嚴，私販越盛，鹽幫也就越聚越大。陳反、趙辯、鄭端等在睦州的聚眾起事，最初正是出於活不下去的饑民，後來才與王仙芝這樣的私鹽首領合流。中間層是唐廷自身的結構性問題：節度使掌兵、掌財、掌任免，與中央只靠宦官監軍相對，朝廷對地方已無實際支配力；各鎮長期欠餉，招募的兵多為市井之徒，遇戰則潰，宿營則劫掠；遇有亂事，饑民、逃戶、散兵與失意軍人匯入叛軍，叛軍的兵源相當一部分其實來自唐軍自身。最深的一層是秩序崩壞的惡性循環：饑荒造成流民，流民聚為盜，盜勢坐大，官軍剿盜又復徵發民力、更增怨望；朝廷對叛軍一味姑息以圖暫安，綏撫不成即改為大軍圍剿，圍剿又逼得流民再度嘯聚。鹽幫首領王仙芝、黃巢原本只是走私商人，官方打壓私鹽正是斷其生路，逼得他們成為公開的反叛者；義軍所打的旗號與官府逼迫百姓的旗號，其實是同一件事的兩面。
causeEn: The reasons for the outbreak can be set out in three layers. The outermost is famine in western Zhejiang and the salt system. In 875 the harvest in the south of the Yangtze failed and hungry people moved in large numbers into eastern Zhejiang; and the Tang maintained salt wells and salt offices in the Mouchang and Wuzhou area, where the monopoly profit was a mainstay of state finance. The salt households served, the ordinary households paid their share, and after the two-tax system was introduced the salt profit and the tax were merged, so the weight fell on small farmers in places that had no salt of their own. Private salt was the seam in this system; the harder the court suppressed it, the larger the trade grew, and the salt bands grew with it. The gathering at Mouchang by Chen Fan, Zhao Bian and Zheng Duan began among people who could not live, and only later merged with a contraband chief such as Wang Xianzhi. The middle layer is a structural problem inside the Tang itself. The military governors held the troops, the revenue and the power of appointment, and stood opposite a centre that had nothing left but eunuch supervisors; the court no longer really governed the localities. The circuits were chronically in arrears, the men they recruited were largely from the towns, and such troops broke at the first real battle and plundered their own camp when quartered; and whenever disorder broke out, the hungry, the tax fugitives, the loose soldiers and the disappointed servicemen all flowed into the rebel bands, so that a good part of the insurgents' manpower in fact came out of the Tang's own forces. The deepest layer is the vicious circle of a collapsing order: famine made the displaced, the displaced banded together as robbers, the robber tide grew, and the government's campaigns against it conscripted the people once more and added to the resentment; the court alternately indulged the rebels to buy quiet and then answered with mass encirclement, and each encirclement drove the displaced to gather again. Wang Xianzhi and Huang Chao were originally only smugglers, and the state's attack on private salt was precisely a destruction of their livelihood that made them rebels in the open. The banner the insurgents fought under and the banner with which the government oppressed the people were two faces of the same thing.
impact: 黃巢之亂對唐室的破壞是結構性的，遠超一場地方叛亂的份量。第一，唐朝最後百年的財政與軍備秩序被打散：州縣倉庫被徵發一空，沿運河與驛道一線的市鎮大批毀於兵火，兩稅的徵收再無固定來源，朝廷只能靠加稅、賣官與括括民間財物維持，社會的再生能力隨之下降。第二，藩鎮割據的局面急劇惡化：趁著平亂，節度使擴兵、擴地，朝廷為換取出兵而許下招討使、兼御史中丞等名銜與節度使自徵鹽利之權，等於把國家的財政與司法權下放給地方；883年之後，唐廷能倚賴的已經不是自己的軍隊，而是沙陀李克用與河東、宣武等幾家藩鎮，中原大部實際處於半獨立狀態。第三，宦官與神策軍的權力進一步坐大，護駕出巡、掌握禁軍、出任監軍成為常態，皇權與宦官、皇權與藩鎮的三方對抗貫穿唐末。第四，首都與政治中心位移：長安在兵火中殘破不堪，其後數十年政治中心與財貨重心逐步東移洛陽、汴州，朱溫正是據汴州而終於907年代唐。第五，黃巢本人留下的文字在後世被讀成亂世的象徵，〈不第後賦〉中「沖天香陣長安道，滿城盡帶黃金甲」兩句傳誦最廣，與韋莊《秦婦吟》等作品一起，成為唐末亂世最著名的文學印記。最後是軍制層面的傳承：亂軍與平亂的經驗，使募兵、驍騎、屯田與軍鎮化在晚唐五代定型，五代十國的割據混戰由此起頭。黃巢之亂的真正產物不是一個新王朝，而是一個再也收拾不起來的舊王朝。
impactEn: The damage Huang Chao's rebellion did to the Tang was structural, and of a very different order from a local rising. First, the fiscal and military order of the Tang's last hundred years was broken up: the granaries of the counties were emptied, the market towns along the canal and the courier roads were largely destroyed by war, the collection of the two-tax lost its regular base, and the court could maintain itself only by adding levies, by selling offices and by searching out the wealth of the people, with a corresponding loss of the capacity of society to regenerate itself. Second, the situation of governors ruling their own territories deteriorated sharply. Profiting from the suppression, the governors enlarged their armies and their territories, and in exchange for putting troops in the field the court granted titles such as commissioner for suppression and censor-in-chief, and the right of the governors to collect the salt revenues themselves; this amounted to handing the state's fiscal and judicial powers down to the localities. After 883 the Tang court no longer leaned on its own armies but on the Shatuo Li Keyong and on a handful of great circuits such as Hedong and Xuanwu, and most of the central plain was effectively half independent. Third, the authority of the eunuchs and the Shence Army grew still further: escorting the emperor, commanding the imperial guards and sitting as supervisors became normal, and the triangular struggle between the throne and the eunuchs, and between the throne and the governors, ran right through the end of the dynasty. Fourth, the capital and the seat of politics shifted: Chang'an was left ruined by the fighting, and over the following decades the centre of politics and of wealth moved east to Luoyang and to Bianzhou, from which Zhu Wen would eventually take the throne in 907. Fifth, Huang Chao's own words came to be read as the emblem of troubled times; the two lines about the fragrant array reaching the sky along the road to Chang'an and the whole city girded with golden armour, from his poem on failing the examination, are the most widely quoted, and together with works such as Wei Zhuang's Lament of the Qin Woman they form the best known literary imprint of the late Tang disorder. Last is a legacy in military institutions: the experience of the fighting on both sides fixed recruitment, the armoured horse, military farms and the militarisation of the circuits in the late Tang and Five Dynasties, and the warfare of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms begins there. The real product of Huang Chao's rebellion was not a new dynasty but an old one that could never be put back together.
result: 廣明元年（880年）十二月，黃巢軍入長安，改元金統，大齊立國；此後三年，是唐廷在形式上仍然存在、實則退保蜀中的三年。883年，李克用率沙陀騎兵入關，於關中大破尚讓所部，黃巢焚長安宮室西走，兵至泰山時眾僅餘數百人，於光啟元年（884年）六月在狼虎谷覆滅，殘首送京師，僖宗於同年十二月還都長安，兩京收復，朝廷宣告平亂。然而收復不等於恢復：義軍殘部仍在尚讓、林言等人手中四處流竄，與官軍在同州、華州一線反覆拉鋸；蔡州奉國軍節度使秦宗權曾降黃巢，此時又反，據蔡州稱帝，直到光啟年間方為官軍所平，部眾被分散編入各鎮，亂局才算收束。從875年睦州起事到最後一批叛軍被收編，前後約十二年。其後的走向已不在這場戰爭之內，但由它決定：平亂的沙陀軍與最早降唐的義軍將領各自據有大鎮，唐廷的兵權、財權與用人權全部旁落，節度使爭地、宦官干政、藩鎮自署官吏，三者互相咬合。到九世紀末，長安已難以重建，帝國的重心完全移到汴州；朱溫終於907年奪位，開五代十國之局。所以黃巢之亂的直接結果是大齊的覆滅與黃巢本人死在泰山狼虎谷，而長遠結果則是唐室的崩解——它既是唐朝的加速器，也是它崩解時的樣本。
resultEn: In the twelfth month of 880 Huang Chao's army entered Chang'an, the era was changed to Jintong, and the Great Qi was proclaimed. The three years that followed were years in which the Tang court still existed in form but had withdrawn in fact to the mountains of Shu. In 883 Li Keyong brought the Shatuo horse through the passes and shattered Shang Rang's main body in Guanzhong; Huang Chao fired the palaces of Chang'an and withdrew west, and by the time he reached Mount Tai he had a few hundred men left with him. In the sixth month of 884 he was destroyed at Langhu Valley, and the remnant of his person was carried to the capital; the emperor returned to Chang'an in the twelfth month of the same year, the two capitals were recovered, and the court announced the suppression of the rebellion. Recovery of the cities, however, was not recovery of the state. The remnants of the insurgents still roamed under men such as Shang Rang and Lin Yan, and the government forces fought back and forth along the line of Tongzhou and Huazhou. Qin Zongquan, governor of the Fengguo Army at Caizhou, who had once surrendered to Huang Chao, rebelled again, proclaimed himself emperor at Caizhou, and was not put down by the court troops until the Guangqi years, his men then being dispersed and absorbed into the various circuits; only then was the disorder at last closed. From the rising at Mouchang in 875 to the incorporation of the last rebel bands, roughly twelve years had passed. What followed lay outside this war, but it had been determined by it: the Shatuo army that had put the rebellion down and the rebel commander who had surrendered earliest each held great territories of their own, the authority of the Tang court over troops, money and appointments had all fallen away, and the governors competing for land, the eunuchs interfering in government and the circuits appointing their own officials locked into one another. By the end of the ninth century Chang'an could no longer be rebuilt and the centre of the empire had moved wholly to Bianzhou; Zhu Wen took the throne in 907 and opened the period of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms. The direct result of Huang Chao's rebellion, then, was the destruction of the Great Qi and the death of Huang Chao himself in Langhu Valley below Mount Tai; the longer result was the dissolution of the Tang. It was both the accelerant of the dynasty's end and the specimen of how the dynasty fell apart.
